CONDITIONS: Entry by arrangement only.  You may enter only at the time arranged with Searle Forestry, and only in the areas agreed. Where harvesting or other operations are underway, entry is also subject to the permission and site induction of the forest manager or harvesting contractor in control of that site. We will arrange this for you.

You enter at your own risk.  You will not hold the landowner, the forest manager, the contractors on site, or Forestry Sales Limited (trading as Searle Forestry) or its licensees liable for any loss, harm or damage suffered.

Report in and report out.  Report to the salesperson on arrival, and again when you leave, to confirm that you and everyone with you are off the property. Agree a check-out time before you leave the vehicle. Cellphone coverage is often poor or absent. If we have not heard from you by the agreed time, we will treat you as missing and begin a search.

Never enter an active work area.  Do not enter any area where felling, breaking out, hauling, processing or loading is underway. Stay at least two tree lengths clear of any felling or hauler operation, and well clear of all ropes under tension. If a machine is working, do not approach it — wait until the operator has seen you, stopped the machine and signalled you in.

Personal protective equipment.  The minimum for any inspection is a high-visibility vest and sturdy boots with good grip. A hard hat is required in any harvesting or felling area. Wear whatever else the site or the induction requires. Tell us in advance if you do not have this gear.

Follow all instructions and signage.  Comply with all instructions given by Searle Forestry, the vendor, the forest manager, the harvesting contractor and their staff, and with all signage, hazard boards and gate notices. Our staff and the site controller may refuse entry to, or remove, any person who does not cooperate.

You are responsible for your party.  You are responsible for everyone who accompanies you. Children must be supervised by an adult at all times, and no person under 16 may enter an operational forestry area.

Vehicles.  Any vehicle you bring must hold a current WoF, be in good working order and be suitable for the conditions. You must hold a current driver licence and have sufficient training and experience for the vehicle and the terrain. Four wheel drive should be engaged while on the property. Keep to formed roads and obvious tracks. Do not venture off the track under any circumstances — steep sidings, bluffs, soft fill and holes can cause serious injury.

Forest roads and log trucks.  Drive with headlights on at all times. Give way to loaded log trucks and all heavy vehicles. Roads are typically one lane — pull over to the cut face (inside) where you can, never onto the outside edge. Where the forest operates RT road call-ups you must carry a radio on the correct channel or be escorted. Never park on a road, a corner, a landing or a skid site.
Speed.  Keep below 30 km/h, and slower on narrow roads or in the wet. Be courteous at all times.
ATVs and side-by-sides.  Operate strictly in accordance with the manufacturer’s instructions and the Agriculture Guideline — Safe Use of ATVs on New Zealand Farms. Helmets must be worn.

Wind and weather.  Do not enter standing forest in strong wind — limbs and whole trees come down. Tracks may be impassable or slippery during and after rain. We may postpone or cancel an inspection on safety grounds at any time.

Fire.  Smoking, open flame and the setting of fires are prohibited in all buildings and anywhere on the property. Do not drive or park on long dry grass or slash — vehicle exhausts and catalytic converters start fires. Observe the current fire season status and any Fire and Emergency New Zealand restrictions advised to you.

Biosecurity.  Arrive with clean boots, tyres and vehicle, free of soil, seed and plant material. Complete any wash-down, spray or hygiene station requirement on arrival and on departure. This includes kauri dieback controls, myrtle rust, wilding conifer seed and other soil-borne diseases.

Livestock and animals.  Take care around all livestock, particularly bulls and stock with young. Keep clear of working dogs. You MUST not bring your own pets onto a farm without permission. Pet dogs can carry and spread diseases or parasites (such as sheep measles) to farm animals if they are not properly treated and vetted.
Gates and fences.  Leave all gates and fences exactly as you find them. Treat every fence as electric and live.

Pest control and toxic baits.  Traps and toxic baits, including 1080 and cyanide, may be in use. Do not touch or handle bait, bait stations or carcasses. Keep dogs in the vehicle — bait and carcasses are lethal to dogs.

Drones.  No drone may be flown without the prior written consent of Searle Forestry and the landowner or forest manager. Any flight must comply with Civil Aviation Rules Part 101, and must not take place over or near any active operation or aerial work.
Firearms and hunting.  Firearms must not be brought onto the property, and no hunting or shooting is permitted. Be aware that permitted hunting by others may be in progress.
Drugs and alcohol.  Zero tolerance. Do not enter the property under the influence of alcohol, drugs, or any medication that may impair you.
No trespass.  Do not go onto neighbouring land at any time.
Damage.  Use best endeavours not to cause damage to the property. If any damage does occur, notify the salesperson or the vendor immediately.
Water.  Do not drink water from taps, tanks or streams unless you are advised it is safe.
Report incidents.  Report any injury, near miss, damage or unsafe condition to your Searle Forestry salesperson immediately, however minor it seems.
